intent: Compare the indexed trends in people killed or injured on British roads for cyclists and car drivers from 2007 to 2016 relative to the 2010-14 average.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Compare the indexed trends for cyclists and car drivers from 2007 to 2016 relative to the 2010-14 average.
For car drivers, the index of people killed or injured fell from 143 in 2007 to 61 in 2016, indicating a strong downward trend relative to the 2010-14 average.

The indexed trends for cyclists and car drivers diverge: cyclists rose overall while car drivers fell sharply, with cyclists starting below and ending above car drivers relative to the 2010-14 average.

units.claim: All 3 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: For cyclists, the index of people killed or injured rose from 85 in 2007 to 110 in 2016, with a peak of 113 in 2011, indicating an overall upward trend relative to the 2010-14 average.
units.computation: Compare first (85), maximum (113), and last (110) values of the cyclists series; note the overall increase from 2007 to 2016.
accept: Cyclists index increased from 85 in 2007 to 110 in 2016.
Cyclists show an overall upward trend.
reject: Cyclists remained below the 2010-14 average throughout.

units.claim: For car drivers, the index of people killed or injured fell from 143 in 2007 to 61 in 2016, indicating a strong downward trend relative to the 2010-14 average.
units.computation: Compare first (143) and last (61) values of the car drivers series; note the overall decrease from 2007 to 2016.
accept: Car drivers index decreased from 143 in 2007 to 61 in 2016.
Car drivers show a strong downward trend.
reject: Car drivers remained above the 2010-14 average throughout.

units.claim: The indexed trends for cyclists and car drivers diverge: cyclists rose overall while car drivers fell sharply, with cyclists starting below and ending above car drivers relative to the 2010-14 average.
units.computation: Compare cyclists and car drivers at start (2007: 85 vs 143) and end (2016: 110 vs 61); note opposite directions and crossover relative to the 100 baseline.
accept: Cyclists and car drivers show opposite trends.
In 2007, car drivers index (143) was higher than cyclists (85).
In 2016, cyclists index (110) was higher than car drivers (61).
Cyclists crossed above car drivers between 2007 and 2016.
reject: Cyclists and car drivers moved in the same direction.
Car drivers remained higher than cyclists throughout.

optional_valid: Cyclists index was below the 2010-14 average (100) in 2007-2009 and above it from 2010 onward.
Car drivers index was above the 2010-14 average until 2011 and below it from 2012 onward.
unsupported_to_avoid: Absolute counts of people killed or injured.
Comparisons involving other road user types not shown.
review_notes: The 2010-14 average is a constant reference line at 100; it is used as a baseline but not treated as a separate trend unit.
The intent asks for a comparison of indexed trends, so the two trend units and one comparison unit cover the analytical operations.
